main_body: Tall Parisian-style brick townhouse: a slate mansard roof with two dormers and a chimney, a brick facade with four windows per floor and a balcony, and a striped-awning shopfront at street level
top_band: Slate blue-grey roof slope, rows ~22-42, with a lighter grey-green flat roof panel above it at rows ~10-22. It ends in an orange eave band at rows 42-46.
evidence: Reading down the middle column, I find the flat roof panel (rows ~10-22) and the slate slope with dormers (rows ~22-42). Next comes a distinct orange eave line (rows ~42-45) with a dark shadow row under it (rows ~46-47), then the brick front face from about row 47 to 142. The roof slope is a clearly visible, tall, textured surface, as in the reference houses, so this is not a front elevation with only a thin hat. The windows have projecting sills and lintels, and the dormers are inset, which gives some recess. No receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The brick has several red-brown tones with individual brick highlights and mortar variation. The slate has stepped blue-greys with a scale pattern. The lit windows carry speckled orange and yellow glints, and the awning, balcony railing and shopfront all show detail. The outlines lean toward the neighbouring material's dark tone (dark brown beside brick, dark blue-grey beside slate) rather than a uniform black. Information per tile is high and comparable to or richer than the references. The only plain area is the small flat-roof panel.
